problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2y+3z=7 \\ x+z=-1 \\ 3z-2x+y=3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & -2 & 3 \\ 1 & b & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -1 \\ c\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}0x-2y+3z=7 \\ x+0y+z=-1 \\ -2x+y+3z=3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=0,\,b=0,\,c=3.$
